name: Reinforcement-learning geosteering and the NORCE/UiS geosteering robot line (RL+PF 'PluRaListic' robot, DQN / Dual-DRL / ADP decision frameworks), 2023-2026
authors_org: Ressi Bonti Muhammad, Apoorv Srivastava, Sergey Alyaev, Reidar B. Bratvold, Daniel M. Tartakovsky, Igor Cheraghi (Kristian Fossum, Hibat Errahmen Djecta on 2026 paper). University of Stavanger (UiS), NORCE Norwegian Research Centre, Stanford; tested in ROGII StarSteer / Geosteering World Cup environments.
year: 2023 (DQN vs ADP, arXiv 2310.04772); 2024 (SPE Norway Subsurface Conf. robot in cloud environment; arXiv 2402.06377); 2025 (Computational Geosciences 29:14; SPE Journal 30(03):995; Muhammad PhD dissertation UiS; Dual-DRL book chapter); 2026 (arXiv 2606.17331, June 2026)

'Decision-Driven Geosteering Under Uncertainty' arXiv 2606.17331 https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17331; dissertation record https://nva.sikt.no/registration/0198cc847557-814be692-c20c-408f-9a2b-7c3f757a6a4a
code_availability: Yes for the 2025 Computational Geosciences paper: https://github.com/ressibm/RLPF (Python: agent.py, network.py, training.py, geosteering_v1.py, naive.py baseline, gr.csv GR log, trained_network weights) and Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/10727358. SPE Journal robot and 2026 Dual-DRL/StarSteer code: not found public [uncertain]; they depend on the proprietary ROGII StarSteer Solo API.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (Computational Geosciences 2025, SPE Journal 2025) plus arXiv preprint (2026). Details of the SPE Journal robot come only from the abstract and JPT synopsis because OnePetro full text was blocked (403).
extreme_summary: A particle filter over the bit's position relative to stratigraphic boundaries (offset plus local dip), weighted by matching GR against an offset/reference log, produces hundreds of interpretations. A DQN-family agent then picks steering actions from that belief. The robot reached a median 77.3% reservoir contact, placing it in the top 14% of GWC human experts, at about 4 s per decision.
task_definition: Sequential decision-making: choose inclination/targetline changes at decision points along a lateral to maximise reservoir contact, given a probabilistic interpretation of where the well is relative to the target layers. The interpretation sub-task (PF) matches our task: estimating the stratigraphic position (TVT-like offset) of the drilled well from GR and a reference log. The RL sub-task has no counterpart in our offline, fixed-trajectory TVT prediction.
inputs: Real-time GR measured along the lateral; GR of an offset/reference (type) well; the trajectory (minimum curvature, DLS ≤3°/100 ft); in the 2026 work, reference stratigraphic interpretations used to fit a KDE of dip-angle increments. The 2025 paper used real GR from the Geosteering World Cup 2020 semifinal, scaled 0-1. No neighbour wells and no multi-log input.
target_parameterisation: PF state is geometric. In the 2025 paper it is the boundary positions b_x of a 3-layer faulted reservoir (20 ft constant thickness, 2-3 faults). In the 2026 paper it is xi = (offset_t, angle_t): vertical offset of the target boundaries plus local dip angle. This amounts to an explicit dip/slope state, the same idea as u = TVT + Z with a dip state in the silver-medal tracker (A15). The RL state is either raw GR (RL-Log) or the PF-estimated distance to the boundaries (RL-Estimation).
output_representation: A particle cloud (128 particles in 2025; 256 in training and 2064 in testing in 2026) giving 'hundreds of most-likely interpretations'. The decision module consumes either the single highest-weight particle or the top-5 particles ('pluralistic'). The final output is a steering action and trajectory, not a TVT curve.
architecture: (1) Bootstrap/sequential-importance-resampling particle filter. Transition: boundary evolution with faults (2025) or KDE-sampled dip-angle increments (2026). Likelihood: Gaussian on the mismatch between measured and reference-predicted GR (sigma = 0.2 on the 0-1 scaled log), data assimilated every 10 ft. (2) Value-based RL: DQN with experience replay and a target network, 3 fully connected ReLU hidden layers (2-4x input width), gamma 0.95, lr 5e-4, 20k episodes, 50k replay, batch 64. 11 discrete actions (inclination change -5° to +5°, inclination held within 86-94°), 10 decision points every 320 ft. The 2026 variant adds a dueling value/advantage 'Dual DRL' network and compares it with Approximate Dynamic Programming. The SPE robot swaps in a targetline action space and realistic DLS constraints inside a StarSteer-like cloud environment.
core_mechanism: Decouple interpretation (PF belief over offset/dip) from decision (RL policy trained on simulated geology). Feeding the RL agent PF estimates instead of raw logs was the key to generalisation. RL-Log collapsed on unseen GR logs, while RL-Estimation stayed robust across log depths and fault counts. Its reservoir contact came within 1-2% of an RL agent given true look-ahead boundaries. For our problem, the transferable pieces are: an explicit dip state with a data-learned (KDE) dip-increment transition prior; keeping several interpretations instead of one; and a belief summary that downstream modules consume.
training_objective: PF: none (Bayesian filtering, hand-set Gaussian GR likelihood). RL: Q-learning TD loss. Reward is 0 inside the reservoir and -1 outside, summed over 32 points (10 ft spacing) per decision. The 2026 paper also reports RMS jerk (steering smoothness) as a stability metric. There is no supervised loss on stratigraphic position.
decoding: Interpretation decode is mode-like: the highest-weight particle, or the top-5 particles passed to the policy. Actions come from the argmax of Q-values. The 2026 ADP baseline uses robust optimisation over the ensemble.
metric_consistent_decode: No. The decode picks the highest-weight particle (MAP-like, mode-seeking), which can raise pooled RMSE in our setting. The PF weighted mean (RMSE-consistent) is available but was not what the robot used.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral drilled so far (causal, filtering only, no smoothing) plus a single reference/typewell. Nothing from multiple wells jointly.
prefix_conditioning: Implicit. The PF is initialised at landing (first 960 ft) with a known position and assimilates GR causally, so earlier interpretation constrains later interpretation through the state. There is no explicit fine-tuning or closed-form correction from known labels.
propose_vs_select: Propose-and-select. The PF proposes many interpretations and the policy selects an action. For us, a PF could slot in as a candidate generator (K particle clusters) for a reranker, or as a cheap CPU ensemble member.
physical_constraints: Constant layer thickness, discrete faults, smooth dip evolution (KDE-sampled increments), DLS limits on the trajectory, and inclination bounds of 86-94°.
dataset: Synthetic geology only. 2025: randomly generated faulted 3-layer models, 320 cells over 3,200 ft, filled with real GR from the Geosteering World Cup 2020 semifinal. SPE robot: synthetic environment modelled on the ROGII GWC (2021 unconventional stage per later citations [uncertain]), 1,000 simulations. 2026: ROGII StarSteer simulator through the Solo API; dataset size not stated.
synthetic_to_real: 100% synthetic geology with real GR textures. GR scaled 0-1 and shifted to target TVD. No sim-to-real alignment stage. The human benchmark ran in a GWC-like synthetic scenario, not on real laterals.
metric_and_performance: Computational Geosciences 2025, reservoir contact: rule-based with 1 particle 54.75%; RL-Log 66.84%; RL-Estimation with 1 particle 88.67% (input MAE 1.29); with 5 particles 88.91%. Oracle RL with true look-ahead >90%. SPE Journal 2025: median 77.3% reservoir contact over 1,000 runs, top 14% of human experts; best run beat every expert. 2026: Dual DRL RMS jerk 0.8 vs ADP 1.32 and DQN 1.38, with the highest median return. None of these papers reports a TVT or stratigraphic-position RMSE.
comparability: Not comparable. The metrics are reservoir contact and steering smoothness, not pooled TVT RMSE on 155 holdout wells. The PF input MAE of 1.29 is in grid cells on a toy 3-layer model.
validation_protocol: Monte Carlo over randomly generated synthetic geologies, plus generalisation tests to unseen GR logs, different log depths and fault counts. There are no real-well holdouts, no spatial grouping and no leaderboard. The human benchmark compares against archived GWC expert results.
inference_budget: RL-Estimation <1 s per scenario (2025). Robot about 4 s per steering decision vs a 2-min stand time (SPE 2025). Training 30 min (RL-Log) to 300-420 min (RL-Estimation), with the PF taking about 95% of compute. A CPU PF at 128-2064 particles fits a Kaggle/rig budget.
repeated_layers: Not addressed explicitly. The synthetic reservoirs have 3 layers of constant thickness, so self-similar repeated bands barely occur. Keeping top-5 interpretations gave only +0.24% contact over the single best particle. PF weights over a GR likelihood are known to struggle to break repeated-band ties without extra evidence.
drift: Handled structurally by the explicit dip/angle state with a KDE transition prior learned from reference interpretations (2026). This is the most relevant piece for our single-straight-line drift mode, but no drift metric is reported.
uncertainty_and_calibration: The particle cloud represents uncertainty and belief-informed control is the point of the work. There is no reliability or calibration analysis of particle weights, and the likelihood sigma is hand-set (0.2).
where_to_use: (a) As a cheap CPU ensemble/blend member or candidate generator: an (offset, dip) PF whose emissions come from our U-Net per-column posteriors or from GR-vs-typewell correlation. (b) As a data-driven prior: fit a KDE of dip increments on real training-well labels, and use it to check and retune the dip process of our synthetic well generator (85% of training data). (c) RL itself has no place in an offline, fixed-trajectory TVT-regression pipeline.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) via the explicit dip state and learned dip prior; weakly band confusion (~51%) via multi-hypothesis particles. The RL component targets no Erudition error mode.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already done or tried: a PF tracker exists in our lineage (Ruby's 7.35 ft PF, A05), and post-hoc sequential decoding over the posterior (forward-backward continuity decode) failed, so a forward-only PF over the same posteriors is unlikely to beat the expectation decode. Genuinely new: (1) a transition prior learned from real interpretations (KDE of dip-angle increments) instead of a hand-set smoothness penalty. Our failed continuity decode used a generic smoothness kernel, and a real-data dip-increment kernel is a different, testable prior. (2) Explicit dip as a state variable rather than per-column independent softmax. (3) The finding that a downstream learner generalises far better when fed belief summaries than raw logs (RL-Estimation vs RL-Log). By analogy, a second-stage model or gate could take posterior summaries (entropy, top-K band positions and weights) as input rather than raw channels. Our failed learned gates may have used rawer features [uncertain]. (4) A pluralistic top-K set is already implicit in our multimodal posterior, and the oracle best-mode decode (4.27 ft) shows the headroom, but the robot line offers no new way to select among the modes.
proposed_experiment: E1 (cheap diagnostic, CPU, about 1 h): fit a KDE of per-step dip increments d(TVT+Z)/dMD, taken at the 345-column resolution, on real training wells. Compare it with the same statistic from our synthetic generator (the synthetic-well code used by experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_data_prep.py / seq_NN_dataset.py). Compare histograms, tail mass and autocorrelation of dip. If the synthetic dips are too smooth or too rough, retune the generator's dip process to match. Retrain 60-epoch ConvNeXt vs the unchanged 60-epoch baseline (5.47 ft) on the same seed, and require a gain beyond the +-0.39 ft noise floor (ideally 2 seeds). E2 (moderate): implement a 2-state (offset, dip) SIR particle filter with the real-data KDE dip transition and emission p(obs | TVT) taken from the per-column softmax dumped by seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all. Add forward-backward smoothing, since the robot's filtering-only setup is weaker for offline use. Decode with the particle-weighted mean, not the top particle. Evaluate pooled RMSE on the 155 holdout wells with a new posterior_pf_decode.py next to posterior_fb_decode.py. Control: the expectation decode on the same dumps, plus the failed fb decode. Also score the PF output as a blend member with ConvNeXt/FastViT at fixed weights chosen on training folds only.
implementation_effort: Low for E1 (statistics script plus one generator knob and retrain). Medium for E2 (PF plus smoother on existing posterior dumps, about 200-300 lines; no network changes).
gpu_cost: E1: one 60-epoch ConvNeXt retrain on the RTX 5060 8 GB (same cost as the existing baseline run). E2: no GPU, since the PF runs on CPU over saved posteriors (1-2k particles x 345 columns x 155 wells takes seconds to minutes).
distillation_compatibility: E1 changes only training data, so it is fully compatible with FastViT KD. E2 is a post-hoc decode on output posteriors and works on teacher or student posteriors equally. The RL policy has no role.
error_correlation_with_ours: Low diversity for E2 if emissions come from our own posteriors, since it re-weights the same evidence. Moderate diversity if emissions are raw GR-vs-typewell correlation, as in the robot's PF, but that PF baseline is much weaker (7.35 ft). E1 changes the model itself, not a blend member.
risk: The RL part is irrelevant to RMSE. The PF part has already been tried in spirit: a forward-backward continuity decode over our posteriors failed, and the 7.35 ft PF is far behind 4.84 ft. Particle weights inherit any miscalibration of the softmax, and MAP-style top-particle decoding raises RMSE. The robot line was validated only on simple synthetic 3-layer or GWC-like geologies with reservoir-contact metrics, so it gives no evidence on band confusion in real repeated-layer stratigraphy. E1 may show that our generator already matches real dip statistics, in which case it yields no gain.
notes: Useful lineage points: the 2026 Djecta et al. paper runs on ROGII StarSteer via the Solo API, the same vendor ecosystem as the Kaggle competition. The GWC 2020 semifinal GR log they use is public (see A19). The robot's '4 s per decision' and 'top 14% of experts' figures are from the SPE abstract and JPT synopsis; full-text details (particle count, exact state, action space) could not be verified because OnePetro returned 403. The key lesson for our pipeline is not RL but the separation of belief and decision, together with the data-learned dip-increment prior.
